paragraphs: In Shemot Rabbah, chapter 29, Baltza asks Rabbi Akiva where earthquakes come from. The supplied locator reads section מ. Hyman traces the statement to Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:3, where Eliyahu asked Rabbi Nehorai, and cites Midrash Tehillim 18:12 and 104:25 as parallels.

notes.text: Hyman supplies chapter 29, section מ, retained literally. The Midrash Rabbah — TE digital Shemot Rabbah 29:9 has Baltza asking Rabbi Akiva; this match does not establish that the supplied letter מ was a printed ט. The Guggenheimer digital Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:2 has Eliyahu asking Nehorai, alongside Hyman’s supplied halakhah 3. The supplied section-letter question remains held.

The section letter on Hyman’s printed page (vol. I, p. 270) resembles a final mem. In the digital Shemot Rabbah the passage is at 29:9, where the rabbis report in Rabbi Hoshaya’s name that Baltza asked Rabbi Akiva. The parallel in Guggenheimer’s Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:2 and the passages in the digital Midrash Tehillim on Psalms 18 and 104 have Eliyahu asking Rabbi Nehorai. The ruined Temple appears in both accounts. The derivation is Hyman’s proposal.
